body:
## Question

How should Ridgeline draw and load entity models?

Using both research tickets, recommend one approach covering:
- How models are drawn, such as an extended entity layer or a separate custom layer.
- How models are loaded, and which glTF subset is supported.
- The download size added, and how the 100-model workload target is met.

This technical call is delegated to the agent under the constraint of no full 3D engine. The user confirms the recommendation and its tradeoffs; they are not asked to choose between APIs.

Blocked by: [Can MapLibre 6.11 draw entity models?](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/issues/72); [Choose a lightweight glTF loading approach](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/issues/73).

Map: [Entity models and representation switching](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/issues/71)

comments.body:
## Resolution

Confirmed by the user on 2026-10-04, together with the heavy-model decision below.

**Recommendation**

Ridgeline draws models in a second custom layer of its own. That layer shares the entity layer's projection code. Each model type is drawn once per material for all of its visible copies, and the enlarged screen size is computed on the CPU each frame. Models load through a small in-house GLB parser that runs on the main thread. There is no new dependency, and the expected addition is about 7 to 11 KB gzip.

**Heavy models (user decision)**

Consumers keep models light. Ridgeline documents a per-model triangle guideline, set from the prototype's measurements, and reports a diagnostic for models above it. Automatic simplified versions for distant models are out of scope for this effort.

**Drawing**

- **A separate model layer that shares one projection path.** Add a custom 3D layer for models directly below the existing entity layer. Move the projection pieces the entity layer already has into one module that both layers use: the flat and globe shader blend, the CPU projection used for picking, and nearest world copy selection. Ridgeline still has exactly one path for projection, precision and the date line. Why a second layer:
  - Models need the opposite draw settings. They are solid surfaces that write depth and hide back faces; today's layer draws see-through geometry without depth writes. Separate layers get the right order: models first, then zones and camera volumes blend over them.
  - The update rhythm differs. Model size and placement change on every camera move; the entity layer rebuilds only when data changes.
  - Failures stay contained. A bad model texture should not hide camera volumes.
  - Resource lifetime differs. Model meshes are shared by many entities and should outlive basemap changes.
- **Who owns what.**
  - The viewport keeps the registry of consumer-registered models, as it does for icons.
  - The entity scene stays the single owner of each entity's representation. It picks icon or model using the threshold and dead zone, hides the icon through map feature state without republishing data, and holds back the airborne dot while the model shows.
  - The model layer draws models. While drawing a frame, it measures each candidate entity's camera distance and size on screen and reports switches to the scene, which applies them on the next frame. The prototype checks that the brief overlap is invisible.
- **Batching: one instanced draw per model type and material.** The parser bakes each part's placement into the mesh and merges parts that share a material. Draw count depends on how many model types are on screen, not on how many entities there are. Off-screen entities are skipped on the CPU.
- **Precision with instancing.** Each frame, the layer moves the high-precision camera matrix to one reference point near the map center on the CPU, and each copy gets a small offset from it. World copies and the date line work as today because each offset is taken from the entity's nearest copy.
- **Screen-size scaling on the CPU.** For each model entity, the layer projects its center and a point one model radius away, using the same CPU projection as picking. The scale is `max(1, target / real size)`: fixed size at mid distance, real size once that is larger. The same measurement gives the camera distance for switching. The pass runs only when MapLibre repaints, so idle maps stay idle. A throwaway Node estimate for 1,100 entities took about 0.4 ms per frame.
- **Orientation.** Heading, plus optional pitch and roll, become one rotation per copy in a local east-north-up frame, after a fixed turn from glTF's axes (+Y up, +Z forward). Terrain exaggeration lifts a model's position but does not stretch its shape.
- **Picking: oriented bounding boxes.** Each model's box is projected with the last drawn frame's scale and world copy, then goes through the existing triangle hit test, terrain occlusion check and depth ordering. Hits report the entity, so the radial picker and selection requests work unchanged. Boxes also hit empty space around thin parts; shape-accurate hits remain a question for the interaction branch. A GPU ID buffer is rejected because it stalls the GPU and ignores terrain depth.
- **Surviving basemap changes and context loss.** Uploaded meshes and textures belong to a cache owned by the viewport and tied to the WebGL context, so a basemap change re-adds the layer without re-uploading. Ridgeline keeps each registered model's original bytes so models can be rebuilt after a WebGL context loss. Ridgeline has no context-loss handling today, so this is new for the whole viewport.

**Loading**

- **An in-house GLB subset parser, not a library.** It turns a file straight into ready-to-upload batches, fetches nothing at runtime, and gives every rejection a named diagnostic tied to the model ID.
- **Accepted:** GLB version 2 with one embedded binary buffer; static triangle lists with positions and optional normals, first texture coordinates and vertex colors; all core data types including `KHR_mesh_quantization` and `KHR_texture_transform`; embedded PNG and JPEG base color images; base color factor and texture, alpha mode and cutoff, double-sided, emissive factor and `KHR_materials_unlit`. Animations, cameras, lights and other texture types are ignored.
- **Rejected by name:** other required extensions (Draco, meshopt, KTX2/Basis, required WebP or AVIF), separate `.gltf` files, external buffers and images, skins, morph targets, sparse data, non-triangle modes. A rejected file leaves its entities as icons with a diagnostic, never a partial model. An image resolver for external textures stays with the consumer API branch.
- **Main thread, ready for a worker later.** Parsing runs at registration, not at switch time. Typical vehicles parsed in 2 to 15 ms in Node. Base color images decode through `createImageBitmap`. The parser is a pure function from bytes to arrays and images, so a worker can be added later without changing the consumer API.

**Lighting and materials**

One fixed directional light in each entity's local frame plus ambient. Color is base color factor × texture × vertex color, plus emissive; unlit materials skip lighting. Solid and cut-out parts draw first and write depth; translucent parts draw afterwards without sorting. Textures get mipmaps. No PBR, normal maps, environment lighting or shadows. Each copy has a reserved tint slot for affiliation, selection and hover; the prototype decides how those look.

**Download size and the 100-model target**

- Parser about 3 to 4 KB gzip, renderer about 4 to 7 KB gzip: about 7 to 11 KB gzip total, no new runtime dependency.
- Today's library build at `61616e4` is 205,453 bytes raw and 58,346 gzip (rechecked 2026-10-03). The 7,476 gzip figure in `docs/performance.md` comes from an older build. Models add about 12 to 19%.
- 1,000 icons stay MapLibre symbols. 100 models cost one draw per visible model type and material plus a small per-frame upload. GPU load depends mostly on triangle count, hence the triangle guideline above.

**Tradeoffs**

- Ridgeline owns a glTF subset parser, a small mesh renderer, its lighting and their tests, in exchange for one projection path, exact control of what loads, named diagnostics, no runtime fetches and no engine dependency.
- Models needing Draco, meshopt, KTX2, animation or external files must be repackaged. Meshopt is the cheapest to add later.
- Simple lighting looks flatter than a PBR viewer. Box picking is coarse around thin shapes. Keeping model bytes costs memory. Very large files can pause the main thread once at registration.

**What the prototype must verify**

1. Frame time with about 100 models of 3 to 5 types plus 1,000 icons on a real integrated and a discrete GPU, flat and globe, including the CPU pass. Use the results to set the triangle guideline.
2. No jitter for meter-scale models at zoom 18 to 20, including across the date line and world copies.
3. Globe: no jump in the zoom 11 to 12 transition, correct up direction, models hidden behind the planet.
4. Terrain contact on slopes at real and enlarged size, with no z-fighting or sinking.
5. Switching: no visible doubling or gap, and the map goes quiet after the camera stops.
6. Lifecycle: basemap change with models loaded, and context loss and restore through `WEBGL_lose_context`.
7. Browser time for parsing, image decoding and upload of the largest samples; revisit the worker above about 50 ms.
8. Orientation and faces after the axis turn, culling, double-sided and translucent parts.
9. Box picking compared with the drawn shape.
10. Layer order of icons, labels, zones and volumes relative to models.
11. Bundle size of the prototype's parser and renderer.

**ADRs**

No conflict with [ADR-0001](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0001-consumer-owned-workflows.md) (consumers supply model bytes; Ridgeline fetches nothing) or [ADR-0002](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-maplibre-extension-access.md) (internal, explicit MapLibre integration). ADR-0003 is not affected.

**Evidence**

- [Can MapLibre 6.11 draw entity models?](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/issues/72): [findings at b1e0fd9](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/blob/b1e0fd97ce45cc37227a07de3e0f6d866e3fbe90/.scratch/entity-models/research/maplibre-model-rendering.md).
- [Choose a lightweight glTF loading approach](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/issues/73): [findings at cc6edca](https://github.com/the-Drunken-coder/Ridgeline/blob/cc6edca4e273378a1a801ad4cddebd753e934cc9/.scratch/entity-models/research/gltf-loading.md).
- Throwaway checks outside the repo on 2026-10-03: current library size, sample part and material counts, CPU-pass estimate in Node. No browser or GPU measurements were made; performance figures are estimates until the prototype.

title: Choose how Ridgeline draws and loads models
